name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
summary: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. These interfaces and languages provide ways of interacting with computer systems and are a common feature across many different platforms within industrial control system environments. Most systems come with some built-in command-line interface and scripting capabilities, for example, macOS and Linux distributions include some flavor of Unix Shell…

strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of Command and Scripting Abuse in ICS

analytics.name: Analytic 2082
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a command-line interpreter (cmd.exe, PowerShell.exe) spawned as a child of an Industrial Control System (ICS) vendor application process, where this parent-child relationship is not part of the documented normal operation of that vendor software or directly spawned processes with a command line parameters containing ICS protocol/Application Programming Interface (API) interaction keywords, from a context not associated with documented automation scripts. analytics.name: Analytic 2083
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a command and scripting interpreter process spawned by an Industrial Control System (ICS) service process, or interactive shell sessions from unexpected Secure Shell (SSH) source Internet Protocol (IP) addresses or an unexpected User Identifier (UID) not associated with recognized ICS automation scripts, deviating from the expected execution baseline. Operational Technology (OT) operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when execution violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/process or tool allowlist, or originates from an unauthorized user/tool, and is tied to an OT asset or follow-on OT-relevant action.
